newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS LOWER ON IMPORT PRESSURE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS LOWER ON IMPORT PRESSURE.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar closed on Tuesday weaker against hard currencies as the central Reserve Bank continued ignoring market cries for help in assuaging import pressure, dealers said.

"Things are going bad. We had a few export receipts but they never even made any impact on the market. The (local) dollar is still going in one direction and there was no sign of the central bank today (to the rescue)," one dealer commented.

Dealers said some market players were holding onto foreign currency reserves so as to protect their positions in case the Reserve Bank continued standing on the sidelines, while others were looking to make a profit by selling at higher exchange rates later.

They were however quick to emphasize that the local currency's present woes had nothing to do with the on-going strike action by civil servants pressing for salary hikes, pointing out that the Zimbabwe dollar was non-tradeable outside the country's borders, and thus not sensitive to foreign sentiment.
At Tuesday's close, the Zimbabwe dollar was quoted at 10.1200/1500 against the U.S. dollar, down from Monday's 10.0900/1200 while against sterling it slipped to 15.7630/8180 from 15.7050/7610.
It was at 6.8540/8770 from 6.8280/8500 versus the mark and fell to 2.2350/2440 from 2.2220/2310 against South Africa's rand. --Stella Mapenzauswa, Harare Newsroom: +263-4 72 52 27/8/9---
